rows.why: He said a bare present for 'I did them now' (engine wrote أملهم); Amal recast with the past عملتهم (she had asked عملتهم؟ at 02:51).

rows.medi_said: would I say صح or مزبوط؟
rows.why: He asked which word to use for 'right' and Amal picked صح as better.
He asked for the word for 'relax' (engine wrote لازم أفتح شوي); she said no and later used ترتاح (11:22); sheet has 'relax | Ertaa7 | ارتاح'.
He said he did not know how to say 'per'; Amal supplied بالأسبوع (her line is timed earlier at 06:10, while he was mid-sentence).

rows.medi_said: أنا أخذت وقت إضافه لـ قهوة
rows.amal_said: إضافة. You dream of إضافة... We say زيادة in spoken.
rows.why: He used the MSA word إضافة; Amal said it is فصحى and spoken is زيادة (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة); he took it.

rows.medi_said: I agree. I don't know how to say I agree.
rows.amal_said: We have a saying-- مظبوط عادي، مظبوط.
rows.why: He said he did not know how to say 'I agree'; her answer is مظبوط (reading of her line is uncertain).
He heard العمر (age/life) as 'command' (أمر); Amal taught the word.

rows.medi_said: Marti. Does this mean my woman?
rows.amal_said: My wife. So it does sound wrong, sir.
rows.why: Putting the -i ending on مرة gives مرتي = my wife; Amal said it sounds wrong and 'technically right but never used' (19:13, 20:18).
rows.proposed_rule: To say 'my first time' do not put -i on مرة (مرتي means my wife); say أول مرة إلي.

rows.amal_said: No. What's the other way to say it? ... أول مرة إلي ... This rule is إلي. The عندي rule is just with مفضل.
rows.why: He used 3andi for 'my first time' and el-awwal after a feminine noun; Amal said no and gave أول مرة إلي and the rule (3ind only with مفضل). He repeated 'awwal mara andi' at 19:19 (same moment).

rows.medi_said: so aglab el marra is most of the time.
rows.amal_said: Yeah, but we don't say that. So أغلب الوقت.
rows.why: He used مرة (occurrence) for 'time' in 'most of the time'; Amal gave أغلب الوقت and explained مرة is occurrence.
For 'the beginning of it' he used awal + min + pronoun; Amal said no, the owner goes on the end (awala/awalha), no min.

rows.amal_said: No, kees is a plastic bag.
rows.why: He tried كيس (also Qissa/Jazan at 30:28) for 'bag'; Amal said kees is a plastic bag and steered him to suitcase/شنتة (sheet: bag | Shanta | شنتة).

rows.amal_said: Does that sound right? ... Akhir shantata means like the end of her bag.
rows.why: aa5er + el- noun means 'the end of', not 'last'; Amal questioned it and explained, he reached شنتة الأخيرة (32:34) and she said Great job.
Another wrong try for 'her last bag' (aa5er + pronoun ending means the end of her ...); Amal said No.
Asked for the second way to say 'her last bag' he tried 'the end'; Amal said not end, then gave آخر شنطة إلها after he said لها.
Amal recast his MSA لها as the spoken إلها on the end of the phrase.
'The end of our program': he put el- and a separate لنا; Amal said No, one way only: آخر برنامجنا (possessive ending, no el-). Words spread over 34:22-34:33.

rows.amal_said: That's her last program. ... No. How do you say the end of?
rows.why: He produced 'her last program' (noun + adjective) when asked for 'the end of'; Amal said No and he reached آخر برنامجها.

rows.amal_said: No. It doesn't mean anything. It means the beginning of their cat.
rows.why: Engine wrote بسيطًا for 'their cat'; awal + noun-with-ending means the beginning of their cat, so he needs the adjective after the noun; Amal said No and explained.
Engine wrote بسطنا (ending -na, 'our'); Amal said 'Their.' to point to -hom; he did not complete the fix.
Engine wrote كسرتها for 'her cup'; taani before a noun with a possessive ending is not the pattern; Amal said No and 'doesn't mean anything'.
Noun + taani gives 'another cup'; for 'second cup' taani goes first; Amal said No, then Great at 39:50 for ثانية كاسا لها.
He did not have the plural of سؤال (sheet has only question | Su2aal | سؤال); Amal said 'very close' and gave أسألتك.
He guessed the plural from the singular; Amal said جواب is one and gave أجوبة.
Feminine plural-form noun takes -t before the owner ending (أجوبة + ك = أجوبتك); Amal recast it.
غير takes عن, not min; Amal said No, then عن، عن (44:33) and 'tied to غير'.

rows.medi_said: wait, there's an N, right? طريقتني؟ No, طريقتي
rows.why: He tried an -ni ending (verb object pronoun) on a noun; Amal said لا and he settled on طريقتي; may be his own self-fix (her لا overlaps his line).

rows.medi_said: راح. This will be راح يكون

rows.why: ykoon must match the feminine مرة; Amal asked if مرة is feminine or masculine and he said راح تكون.
rows.english: this will be the last time

Amal answered 'ما عنا' (twice, 57:15 and 57:18) for 'we don't have'; ma + 3ind form.
